page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ce4.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor running at 3.2 GHz. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of x86_64 system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and it does not include any GPU accelerators. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.ce4.xlarge primarily in the lower performance tiers. Both single-core and multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests register in the bottom 25% of all tested servers. Memory bandwidth performance is also constrained, with large-block read-only operations falling into the bottom 10% at 22.44 GB/sec, and write operations in the bottom 25% at 14.99 GB/sec. However, the instance demonstrates average performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 25.96 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 9.53 GB/sec, alongside average text generation speeds of 80.49 tokens/sec for small 135M parameter language models.

Given its older Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 hardware profile, the ecs.ce4.xlarge offers a qualitative cost-efficiency model centered on high memory density rather than raw compute throughput. The tradeoff involves a generous 32.0 GB memory allocation paired with weak CPU and memory bandwidth performance. This profile makes the instance suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand high-speed processing, such as caching layers, lightweight database operations, basic web serving, or legacy enterprise applications requiring a larger memory footprint without high CPU utilization.
